caption: Retail Lending
vo: A home loan touches a lot of hands. Here's one from the client's first call all the way to disbursement, with every hand-off, check and approval in one record.

caption: Anika Gopaul calls about a home loan
vo: It starts with a phone call. Anika Gopaul wants a home loan.

caption: Sign in as Sophie Lagesse — Loans Executive
vo: Sophie Lagesse, a loans executive, takes the call. She logs the enquiry while Anika is still on the line, so nothing gets lost between the phone and the system.

caption: What she wants: a real-estate loan of MUR 4.5 million over 20 years
vo: What does Anika want? A real-estate loan of four point five million rupees, over twenty years.

caption: Routing assigns lending enquiries round the loans team — this one stays with Sophie
vo: Routing shares lending enquiries round the loans team. This one stays with Sophie, and the first-contact SLA clock starts now.

caption: She qualifies on the call — drag the enquiry to Qualified, then Converted
vo: She qualifies Anika right there on the call, and drags the enquiry to Qualified, then Converted. That one move creates the client, the KYC case and the loan application.

caption: The loan application is waiting in Retail Lending
vo: And here's the application, already at Pre-qualified, with the amount and tenure carried over.

caption: Application captured needs the client's income and the property value
vo: Sophie tries to move it on, but the board pushes back. Application captured needs Anika's income and the property value, and it says so.

caption: Open the record from the message and complete it
vo: So she opens the record right from the message, and fills in the purpose, income, existing repayments and property value.

caption: Tick the client's consent to the MCIB credit bureau check
vo: Then the consent for the MCIB credit check. No consent, no credit report.

caption: The CRM prices the loan and checks eligibility by itself
vo: Now watch. The CRM prices the loan by itself. Genesis PLR plus the product margin gives the rate, then the monthly instalment and the total interest.

caption: Loan-to-value, debt-service ratio and eligibility
vo: Loan-to-value, debt-service ratio and eligibility, too. Even who approves it. Up to five million, that's the Loans Manager.

caption: Now Application captured is accepted
vo: This time the move goes through. The MCIB report is pulled, and Anika gets a status email.

caption: Documents pending: the client is emailed the document checklist
vo: At Documents pending, Anika is emailed the checklist of what she needs to send in.

caption: The Docs tab shows the checklist for a real-estate loan
vo: The Docs tab shows what's in, and what's still missing.

caption: Send the client a secure upload link
vo: Sophie sends a secure upload link. No sign-in, and Anika only sees what's still needed.

caption: Her uploads land on this application and tick off the checklist
vo: Her uploads land right here, ticking off the list.

caption: Documents in: Documents complete, then on to credit
vo: Documents in, so it's Documents complete, then on to credit. Credit appraisal only takes an eligible application, or one with its policy exceptions on record.

caption: The credit analyst picks up the application
vo: Now credit picks it up. Same record, a different person, a different form.

caption: Sign in as Nadia Peerbux — Credit Analyst
vo: Meet Nadia Peerbux, our credit analyst. Nadia appraises the risk and recommends a decision.

caption: The MCIB credit report is already on the application
vo: The MCIB report is already waiting for Nadia. Score, rating and reference, straight from the bureau.

caption: Switch to the Credit appraisal workbench form
vo: Nadia switches to the credit appraisal form, and records the risk grade, the recommendation and the conditions.

caption: Credit approval: the request goes to the right authority for the amount
vo: Moving to Credit approval sends the request to the right authority for the amount.

caption: MUR 4.5 million: the Loans Manager decides
vo: At four point five million, that's the Loans Manager. Four eyes, so whoever sent it can never approve it.

caption: Sign in as Rajiv Doorgakant — Manager, Loans & Fixed Income
vo: So let's sign in as Rajiv Doorgakant, Manager, Loans and Fixed Income. He approves loans up to five million rupees.

caption: Tools ▸ Approvals: grade, DSR, LTV and the analyst's recommendation on one card
vo: In his approvals inbox, everything he needs is on one card. The grade, the DSR, the LTV and Nadia's recommendation. No chasing files, no digging through email. He can decide right here.

caption: Approved — the application moved itself to Offer issued
vo: Approved. And the application moves itself to Offer issued, with the decision, date and PLR recorded.

caption: The offer letter was generated and filed here
vo: The offer letter is generated and filed, and Anika is emailed. If she doesn't accept in thirty days, it lapses.

caption: The client signs the offer — back to the loans executive
vo: Anika signs the offer, and it's back to Sophie, to record the signature, the security and the amount to disburse.

caption: Sign in as Sophie Lagesse — Loans Executive
vo: So we're signed in as Sophie again. Let's pick it up where the offer left off.

caption: Valuation, notary, fixed charge, life and building insurance
vo: She ticks off the security. Valuation, notary, the fixed charge, and life and building insurance, all in place.

caption: Signed offer: move to Offer accepted, then Security & insurance
vo: Then the application moves to Offer accepted, then Security and insurance. Anika gets a status email at each milestone.

caption: Ready for disbursement needs perfected security and an approved KYC
vo: But Ready for disbursement needs perfected security and an approved KYC. Anika's KYC case is still open, so the move is refused.

caption: Finish the KYC case that was opened at conversion
vo: Remember the KYC case from conversion? Let's finish it.

caption: ID, proof of address and source of funds are on file
vo: ID, proof of address and source of funds are all on file. Sophie ticks the checks and the FATCA status.

caption: Move it to Screening: sanctions and PEP lists are checked automatically
vo: At Screening, sanctions and PEP lists are checked automatically, and the result and its reference go straight onto the case.

caption: Clear — Pending approval sends the case to Compliance
vo: She's clear, so Pending approval sends it to Compliance. High-risk clients would go to the MLRO.

caption: Compliance signs off the KYC case
vo: Four eyes again. Sophie can't approve her own client.

caption: Sign in as Fatima Hossenbux — Compliance Officer
vo: So Fatima Hossenbux, our compliance officer, signs it off.

caption: Tools ▸ Approvals: the KYC case with its risk score and rating
vo: In her approvals inbox, the KYC case comes with its risk score and rating, so she knows what she's signing before she approves.

caption: KYC approved — the loans executive tries again
vo: KYC approved. Sophie tries again.

caption: Sign in as Sophie Lagesse — Loans Executive
vo: Back as Sophie, she moves the application to Ready for disbursement. This time, the gate lets it through, because both the security and the KYC are in order.

caption: An approval request goes to the operations checker
vo: Before any money moves, it's maker-checker. Whoever requests a disbursement can't approve it.

caption: Sign in as Ritesh Seewoo — Operations Checker
vo: That's Ritesh Seewoo, the operations checker. The second pair of eyes.

caption: Tools ▸ Approvals: the disbursement request, with security and KYC status
vo: He sees the disbursement request with the security and KYC status right beside it. Everything checks out, so he approves.

caption: The loan is booked in the core loan system
vo: The loan is booked in the core loan system, and the LMS account number comes back onto the application.

caption: The loans executive closes the application as Disbursed
vo: Sophie closes it as Disbursed.

caption: Sign in as Sophie Lagesse — Loans Executive
vo: One last time as Sophie. She drags the application to Disbursed. Now, this is where a lot of systems stop, and servicing starts from scratch somewhere else. Not here. Let's look at what happened next.

caption: Related: the loan account was opened automatically
vo: The loan account opened automatically. Loan Servicing now tracks instalments, arrears and the balance.

caption: One record, the whole journey
vo: One record, the whole journey. Five people worked the same application, with no re-keying, and every step audited. Next, commercial lending.
